Correlation analysis

```{r}
# Better approach - separate treatment for different variable types
library(psych)

# Prepare the data
my.vars.prepared <- my.vars

# Convert ordered factors to numeric (these are ordinal)
ordered_vars <- sapply(my.vars.prepared, is.ordered)
for(var in names(my.vars.prepared)[ordered_vars]) {
  my.vars.prepared[[var]] <- as.numeric(my.vars.prepared[[var]])
}

# Handle character variables
# kar_nejlepsi: binary variable (Ano/Ne)
if("kar_nejlepsi" %in% names(my.vars.prepared)) {
  my.vars.prepared$kar_nejlepsi <- as.numeric(as.factor(my.vars.prepared$kar_nejlepsi))
}

# spec_hlavni: nominal categorical (10 levels) - might want to exclude from correlation
# gender: nominal categorical (3 levels)
if("gender" %in% names(my.vars.prepared)) {
  my.vars.prepared$gender <- as.numeric(as.factor(my.vars.prepared$gender))
}

# You might want to exclude spec_hlavni since it's purely nominal with many categories
my.vars.for_cor <- my.vars.prepared[, !names(my.vars.prepared) %in% "spec_hlavni"]

print("Variables for correlation analysis:")
print(names(my.vars.for_cor))

# Compute correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(my.vars.for_cor, use = "complete.obs")
print("Correlation matrix:")
print(round(cor_matrix, 3))

# Create a more readable correlation matrix
library(corrplot)

# Compute correlations
cor_matrix <- cor(my.vars.for_cor, use = "pairwise.complete")
# Reorder the correlation matrix to put krize_rep first
desired_order <- c("krize_rep", setdiff(colnames(cor_matrix), "krize_rep"))
cor_matrix <- cor_matrix[desired_order, desired_order]

# Visualize the correlation matrix
corrplot(cor_matrix, method = "color", type = "upper", 
         diag = FALSE, # Explicitly exclude diagonal
         tl.cex = 0.8, tl.col = "black", order="original")

# Or create a simple heatmap
# Create heatmap with smaller labels
heatmap(cor_matrix, 
        symm = TRUE,
        cexRow = 0.4,     # Row label size (smaller = more readable)
        cexCol = 0.4,     # Column label size
        margins = c(10, 10), # Increase margins to fit labels
        Rowv = NA,        # Disable row clustering
        Colv = NA)  # Disable column clustering

```

The Fruchterman-Reingold algorithm visualizing correlation networks

```{r}
library(igraph)

# Set threshold
threshold <- 0.15

library(igraph)

# Create adjacency matrix with ABSOLUTE values
adj_matrix <- abs(cor_matrix_ordered)
adj_matrix[adj_matrix < threshold] <- 0
diag(adj_matrix) <- 0

# Create graph
cor_graph <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adj_matrix, 
                                        mode = "undirected", 
                                        weighted = TRUE)

# Get edge list and extract original correlation values
edge_list <- get.edgelist(cor_graph)
original_correlations <- sapply(1:nrow(edge_list), function(i) {
  v1 <- edge_list[i, 1]
  v2 <- edge_list[i, 2]
  return(cor_matrix_ordered[v1, v2])
})

# Add original correlations as edge attribute
E(cor_graph)$original_cor <- original_correlations

# Apply Fruchterman-Reingold layout
set.seed(123)
fr_layout <- layout_with_fr(cor_graph)

# Plot with edge width proportional to correlation strength
plot(cor_graph,
     layout = fr_layout,
     vertex.size = 12,
     vertex.color = ifelse(V(cor_graph)$name == "krize_rep", "gold", "lightsteelblue"),
     vertex.label.cex = 0.6,
     vertex.label.color = "black",
     edge.width = abs(E(cor_graph)$original_cor) * 8,  # Width based on absolute correlation
     edge.color = ifelse(E(cor_graph)$original_cor > 0, "red", "blue"),
     main = "Correlation Network - Edge Width = Correlation Strength")

legend("topright", 
       legend = c("Positive correlation", "Negative correlation", "Thicker = Stronger"),
       col = c("red", "blue", "black"),
       lty = c(1, 1, 1),
       lwd = c(2, 2, 4),
       cex = 0.8)
```

Multinomial Regression using nnet package 

```{r}
# learning multinomial regression model
library(nnet)
# Combine all predictor variables
all.predictors <- c(likert.vars, ordinal.vars, boolean.vars, categorical.vars)
# Create formula using reformulate
formula <- reformulate(termlabels = all.predictors, response = dependent.var)

# Fit multinomial logistic regression
# decay = 0.01
# decay = 1.8
model <- multinom(formula, data = my, decay = 1.8, # L2 penalty parameter 
                  maxit = 1000 # Increase iterations
                  )
```

The problem of this model is that it uses very few respondents for learning

```{r}
model_frame_used <- model.frame(model)
# Now we can see it uses only 260 data vectors, which is much less than nrow(my), which is 878.
print(nrow(model_frame_used))
# multinom doesn't have an option for variable-specific sample sizes. 
# This is a fundamental limitation of how regression models work. 
# Multiple imputation is the proper statistical solution to use all available information while maintaining valid inference, use e.g. mice ...
```

We remove variables with too much missingness rather than rows

```{r}
library(dplyr)
# Filter to only existing variables
valid.predictors <- all.predictors[all.predictors %in% names(my)]
missing_pct <- my %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(valid.predictors)) %>%
  summarise_all(~mean(is.na(.)) * 100)
# Keep only variables with <10% missing
good_vars <- names(missing_pct)[missing_pct < 10]
# These are variables that are frequently missing
print(setdiff(all.predictors,good_vars))
```

Now we learn model with variables that do not have high missingness

```{r}
formula_reduced <- reformulate(termlabels = good_vars, response = dependent.var)
# Fit multinomial logistic regression
# decay = 0.01
# decay = 1.8
model <- multinom(formula_reduced, data = my, decay = 1.8, # L2 penalty parameter 
                  maxit = 1000 # Increase iterations
                  )
model_frame_used <- model.frame(model)
# Now we can see it uses only 747 data vectors, which is not so much less than nrow(my), which is 878.
print(nrow(model_frame_used))
BIC(model)
```

Quick systematic approach to find significance of variables using the model likelihood ratio (LR)
Note: 
for decay=1.8 found by caret 10F CV no variable is significant 
for decay=0 two variables are significant: obor_rychly and vek

```{r}

# Enhanced version with significance stars
test_variable_significance_enhanced <- function(full_model, data, decay=1.8) {
  # Get all variables used in the model
  model_vars <- all.vars(formula(full_model))
  complete_data <- data[complete.cases(data[, model_vars]), ]
  
  print(paste("Using", nrow(complete_data), "complete observations out of", nrow(data)))
  
  # Refit full model on complete data
  full_model_complete <- multinom(formula(full_model), data = complete_data, trace = FALSE, 
                                  decay = decay, # L2 penalty parameter 
                                  maxit = 1000 # Increase iterations
  )
  full_loglik <- logLik(full_model_complete)
  
  # Get predictor variables (excluding response)
  response_var <- all.vars(formula(full_model))[1]
  predictor_vars <- setdiff(all.vars(formula(full_model)), response_var)
  
  results <- data.frame(
    Variable = character(),
    LR_Chisq = numeric(),
    Df = numeric(),
    P_value = numeric(),
    Significance = character(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (var in predictor_vars) {
    cat("Testing variable:", var, "\n")
    
    # Fit reduced model on the SAME complete data
    reduced_formula <- update(formula(full_model), paste("~ . -", var))
    reduced_model <- multinom(reduced_formula, data = complete_data, trace = FALSE,
                              decay = decay, # L2 penalty parameter 
                              maxit = 1000 # Increase iterations
    )
    reduced_loglik <- logLik(reduced_model)
    
    # Calculate LR statistic
    lr_stat <- -2 * (as.numeric(reduced_loglik) - as.numeric(full_loglik))
    df_diff <- attr(full_loglik, "df") - attr(reduced_loglik, "df")
    p_value <- pchisq(lr_stat, df = df_diff, lower.tail = FALSE)
    
    # Add significance stars
    sig_stars <- ifelse(p_value < 0.001, "***",
                 ifelse(p_value < 0.01, "**",
                 ifelse(p_value < 0.05, "*",
                 ifelse(p_value < 0.1, ".", ""))))
    
    results <- rbind(results, data.frame(
      Variable = var,
      LR_Chisq = round(lr_stat, 3),
      Df = df_diff,
      P_value = round(p_value, 5),
      Significance = sig_stars
    ))
  }
  
  # Order by p-value (ascending)
  results <- results[order(results$P_value), ]
  
  # Reset row names
  rownames(results) <- NULL
  
  return(results)
}

print("Output with significance indicators:")
enhanced_results <- test_variable_significance_enhanced(model, my, decay=0)
print(enhanced_results)
print("Significance codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1")

```

```{r}
library(caret)
set.seed(123)
train_control<- trainControl(method="cv", number=10, savePredictions = TRUE)
tune_grid <- expand.grid(decay = seq(0, 2, by = 0.2))
model_10f <- train(formula_reduced, 
                       data=my, 
                       trControl=train_control, 
                       method="multinom", 
                       na.action = na.omit, 
                       tuneGrid = tune_grid)
# Look at the CV performance
print(model_10f)
model_10f$results

# Look at the final model
summary(model_10f$finalModel)

# Variable importance from the CV model
# varImp(olr_model_10f)
# plot(varImp(olr_model_10f), top = 10)

# Get predictions from finalModel (747 records)
final_predictions <- predict(model_10f$finalModel)
# The finalModel used 747 out of 806 records from trainingData
# We need to figure out which 747 records were actually used
training_data <- model_10f$trainingData
# Check if there are any additional NAs that were removed
complete_rows <- complete.cases(training_data[, -ncol(training_data)])  # Exclude .outcome column
actual_outcomes <- training_data$.outcome[complete_rows]

# Create confusion matrix
cm <- confusionMatrix(final_predictions, actual_outcomes)
print(cm)
print.cfM(cm$table, file="cfM-mlr-10f.pdf")
```

```{r}
library(car)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Get Anova results
anova_results <- Anova(model_10f$finalModel, type = "II")

# Create data frame with variable names and importance
importance_df <- data.frame(
  FullTerm = rownames(anova_results),
  Importance = anova_results$`LR Chisq`,
  P_value = anova_results$`Pr(>Chisq)`
)

# Clean variable names: remove backticks AND polynomial terms
importance_df$BaseVariable <- gsub("`", "", importance_df$FullTerm)  # Remove backticks first
importance_df$BaseVariable <- gsub("\\.L|\\.Q|\\.C|\\^[0-9]+", "", importance_df$BaseVariable)  # Then remove polynomial terms

# Aggregate by base variable (sum the chi-square statistics)
combined_importance <- importance_df %>%
  group_by(BaseVariable) %>%
  summarise(
    TotalImportance = sum(Importance),
    MinPValue = min(P_value),
    NumTerms = n(),  # Number of polynomial terms combined
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(TotalImportance))

# Plot combined importance
top_n <- 10
ggplot(combined_importance[1:top_n, ], 
       aes(x = reorder(BaseVariable, TotalImportance), y = TotalImportance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Variable", y = "Combined LR Chi-square", 
       title = paste("Top", top_n, "Variables (Combined Polynomial Terms)")) +
  theme_minimal()

# Show the cleaned results
print(head(combined_importance, 15))

```

```{r}
    colnames(my.tab) <- c("Yes, significant crisis", 
                     "Yes, minor crisis", 
                     "I don't know", 
                     "No, there is no crisis")
    if (var.name=="obor_tlak"){
      rownames(my.tab) <- c("Definitely/Rather not", 
                   "I don't know", 
                   "Rather yes", 
                   "Definitely yes")
    }
    if (var.name=="obor_dotovany" | var.name=="obor_medializ" | var.name=="obor_rychly"){
      rownames(my.tab) <- c("Definitely not", 
                   "Rather not", 
                   "I don't know", 
                   "Rather yes", 
                   "Definitely yes")
    }
    if (var.name=="kar_citace"){
      rownames(my.tab) <- c("Up to 100", "Up to 500", "Up to 1000", "Up to 5000", "More than 5000")
    }

    mosaicplot(my.tab,col = c(4,6,7,8),main="", dir=c("h","v"), las=2, 
             xlab="Is there a replication crisis?", ylab=eng.var.name)
  dev.off()
}

# Restore original settings
par(old_par)
```

Ordinal logistic regression using the polr 

```{r}
library(MASS)
olr_model <- polr(data=my, formula = formula_reduced, method = "logistic", Hess=TRUE)
BIC(olr_model)
```

Computing p-values for all variables of the model

```{r}
# Quick systematic approach to find significant variables:
library(car)
print("Significance of all variables:")
Anova(olr_model, type = "II")

if (FALSE) {
  # This works only for data with no missing values, which is NOT our case.
  print("\nBackward selection to find parsimonious model:")
  final_model <- step(olr_model, direction = "backward", test = "Chisq")
  summary(final_model)
}
```

Computing p-values independently for all but contrast value of all variables

```{r}
## store the coefficients table without the zeta coefficients
ctable <- coef(summary(olr_model))
ctable <- ctable[1:(nrow(ctable) - 3), ]
## calculate and store p values
p <- pnorm(abs(ctable[, "t value"]), lower.tail = FALSE) * 2
## combined table
ctable <- cbind(ctable, "p value" = p)
ctable <- ctable[order(ctable[,"p value"]),]
nms <- rownames(ctable[ctable[,"p value"] <= 0.05,])

# variables with at least one significant coefficient for its values
unique(substr(nms,1,nchar(nms)-2))
```

Example of testing of a variable's significance by removing it from the model

```{r}
test.var <- "obor_dotovany"
# Get all terms from your original formula
all_terms <- attr(terms(formula_reduced), "term.labels")
# Remove the term you don't want
reduced_terms <- all_terms[!grepl(test.var, all_terms)]
# Rebuild formula
response_var <- all.vars(formula_reduced)[1]  # assumes first variable is response
reduced_formula <- as.formula(paste(response_var, "~", paste(reduced_terms, collapse = " + ")))
reduced_model <- polr(reduced_formula, data = my)
anova.res <- anova(reduced_model, olr_model)
# if the value is <= 0.05 the model with test.var is better
anova.res$`Pr(Chi)`[2]
```

Caret package 10-fold cross-validation

```{r}
library(caret)
set.seed(123)
train_control<- trainControl(method="cv", number=10, savePredictions = TRUE)
olr_model_10f <- train(formula_reduced, data=my, trControl=train_control, method="polr", 
                       na.action = na.omit, tuneGrid = data.frame(method = "logistic"))
# Look at the CV performance
print(olr_model_10f)
olr_model_10f$results

# Look at the final model
summary(olr_model_10f$finalModel)

# Variable importance from the CV model
# varImp(olr_model_10f)
# plot(varImp(olr_model_10f), top = 10)

# Confusion matrix from CV predictions
cm <- confusionMatrix(olr_model_10f$pred$pred, olr_model_10f$pred$obs)
print(cm)
print.cfM(cm$table, file="cfM-olr-10f.pdf")

library(car)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Get Anova results
anova_results <- Anova(olr_model_10f$finalModel, type = "II")

# Create data frame with variable names and importance
importance_df <- data.frame(
  FullTerm = rownames(anova_results),
  Importance = anova_results$`LR Chisq`,
  P_value = anova_results$`Pr(>Chisq)`
)

# Clean variable names: remove backticks AND polynomial terms
importance_df$BaseVariable <- gsub("`", "", importance_df$FullTerm)  # Remove backticks first
importance_df$BaseVariable <- gsub("\\.L|\\.Q|\\.C|\\^[0-9]+", "", importance_df$BaseVariable)  # Then remove polynomial terms

# Aggregate by base variable (sum the chi-square statistics)
combined_importance <- importance_df %>%
  group_by(BaseVariable) %>%
  summarise(
    TotalImportance = sum(Importance),
    MinPValue = min(P_value),
    NumTerms = n(),  # Number of polynomial terms combined
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(TotalImportance))

# Plot combined importance
top_n <- 10
ggplot(combined_importance[1:top_n, ], 
       aes(x = reorder(BaseVariable, TotalImportance), y = TotalImportance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Variable", y = "Combined LR Chi-square", 
       title = paste("Top", top_n, "Variables (Combined Polynomial Terms)")) +
  theme_minimal()

# Show the cleaned results
print(head(combined_importance, 15))
```


```{r}
library(car)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Get Anova results
anova_results <- Anova(olr_model_10f$finalModel, type = "II")

# Create data frame with variable names and importance
importance_df <- data.frame(
  FullTerm = rownames(anova_results),
  Importance = anova_results$`LR Chisq`,
  Df = anova_results$Df,
  P_value = anova_results$`Pr(>Chisq)`
)

# Clean variable names: remove backticks AND polynomial terms
importance_df$BaseVariable <- gsub("`", "", importance_df$FullTerm)
importance_df$BaseVariable <- gsub("\\.L|\\.Q|\\.C|\\^[0-9]+", "", importance_df$BaseVariable)

# Aggregate by base variable - sum chi-square AND degrees of freedom
combined_importance <- importance_df %>%
  group_by(BaseVariable) %>%
  summarise(
    TotalLRChisq = sum(Importance),
    TotalDf = sum(Df),
    MinPValue = min(P_value),
    NumTerms = n(),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Calculate proper p-value using combined chi-square and df
    CombinedPValue = pchisq(TotalLRChisq, df = TotalDf, lower.tail = FALSE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(TotalLRChisq))

# Show results
print(head(combined_importance, 15))
```
```{r}
# Using the combined_importance from Option 1
combined_importance$Significance <- ifelse(combined_importance$CombinedPValue < 0.001, "p < 0.001",
                                    ifelse(combined_importance$CombinedPValue < 0.01, "p < 0.01", 
                                    ifelse(combined_importance$CombinedPValue < 0.05, "p < 0.05", "p ≥ 0.05")))

top_n <- 10
ggplot(combined_importance[1:top_n, ], 
       aes(x = reorder(BaseVariable, TotalLRChisq), y = TotalLRChisq, fill = Significance)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Variable", y = "Combined LR Chi-square", 
       title = paste("Top", top_n, "Most Important Variables"),
       fill = "Significance Level") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("p < 0.001" = "darkgreen", "p < 0.01" = "green", 
                               "p < 0.05" = "orange", "p ≥ 0.05" = "red")) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Calculate Spearman correlation (better for ordinal data)
but Pearson correlation is actually almost the same

```{r}
# Get CV predictions
cv_predictions <- olr_model_10f$pred

spearman_cor <- cor(as.numeric(cv_predictions$pred), as.numeric(cv_predictions$obs), 
                    method = "spearman")
print(paste("Spearman correlation:", round(spearman_cor, 3)))

pearson_cor <- cor(as.numeric(cv_predictions$pred), as.numeric(cv_predictions$obs), 
                    method = "pearson")
print(paste("Pearson  correlation:", round(pearson_cor, 3)))


# Calculate for each fold
library(dplyr)
fold_correlations <- cv_predictions %>%
  group_by(Resample) %>%
  summarise(
    Spearman = cor(as.numeric(pred), as.numeric(obs), method = "spearman"),
    Pearson = cor(as.numeric(pred), as.numeric(obs), method = "pearson"),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

print("Correlations by fold:")
print(fold_correlations)
print(paste("Mean Spearman correlation:", round(mean(fold_correlations$Spearman), 3)))
print(paste("Mean Pearson correlation:", round(mean(fold_correlations$Pearson), 3)))
```

Multinomial Regression using glmnet package 

```{r}
# Create model matrix for glmnet
X <- model.matrix(terms(model_frame_used), model_frame_used)[, -1]
# Fit glmnet 
library(glmnet)
cv_glmnet <- cv.glmnet(X, actual_y, family = "multinomial", alpha = 1)
glmnet_model <- glmnet(X, actual_y, family = "multinomial", lambda = cv_glmnet$lambda.min)
# Get model coefficients
coef(glmnet_model)

```



```{r}
  # 1. CLASS PREDICTIONS (most common for confusion matrix)
  class_pred <- predict(glmnet_model, newx = X, s = cv_glmnet$lambda.min, type = "class")
  class_pred_factor <- as.factor(class_pred[, 1])
  # Result: matrix with 1 column containing factor levels
  # 2. PROBABILITY PREDICTIONS
  prob_pred <- predict(glmnet_model, newx = X, s = cv_glmnet$lambda.min, type = "response")
  prob_matrix <- prob_pred[, , 1]  # Extract the probability matrix
  # Result: array with probabilities for each class
  # Get class names
  class_names <- dimnames(prob_matrix)[[2]]
  # compare predictions with actual values in data
  library(caret)
  class_pred_factor <- factor(class_pred_factor, levels = levels(actual_y))
  cm <- confusionMatrix(data = class_pred_factor, reference = as.factor(actual_y))
  print.cfM(cm$table, file="cfM-glmnet.pdf")
```
